his_words: forme de dim 0; ensemble discret; ens quotient
statement: A dimension-zero form is a discrete set. A model is a set L equipped with an equivalence relation, and its associated form is L/~. A recursive geometry in dimensions <=n is proposed, not constructed in these opening paragraphs.
reconstruction: The quotient notation L/~ is modern notation for his explicit quotient. No higher-dimensional category is supplied here.
check_reason: The entry preserves the form/model distinction and confines the absence of a completed recursion to the supplied early pages.

his_words: ensemble des lieux; ensemble des segments; lieux intérieurs
statement: The revised data are sets L,S, a map I↦support(I)⊂L, and a map δ:S→P₂(L) with δI⊂support(I). Regular lieux are the union of support(I) minus δI; all other lieux are singular. These data alone do not specify a topology.
reconstruction: support(I) denotes his tilde I. The abandoned extra relations in scans2–3 are excluded from the live data.
check_reason: All maps and the definition of regularity occur explicitly; the earlier L₀ data are within a deleted block.

statement: F1: for each segment I, each endpoint x∈δI and each z∈support(I)∖{x}, exactly one segment J has support(J)⊂support(I) and δJ={x,z}. In particular Ixy=Iyx=I for δI={x,y}.
reconstruction: This is an axiom, not an unproved theorem. It says nothing by itself about arbitrary internal pairs.
check_reason: The entry correctly restricts uniqueness to subsegments incident to an endpoint.

statement: F2 originally assumes every segment has nonempty interior. For z internal to I with δI={x,y}, Ixz∩Iyz={z}, and every subsegment of I incident to z lies on one of these two sides. The later general network notion admits empty interiors and names the original nonemptiness condition divisibility.
reconstruction: The uncertain marginal verb is not resolved. Admission of reduced graphs supplies independent textual evidence of the changed scope.
check_reason: The entry separates the retained separation conditions from the abandoned universal divisibility condition.

his_words: Axiome des branches; relation d’équivalence; compléter F3
statement: For I,J incident to x, F3 gives initial subsegments which either coincide or meet only at x. The intended relation I~xJ is existence of a common nontrivial initial subsegment. The added F3′ requires common smaller initial segments within a fixed segment, so that these germs are transitive and their classes define Bx. In the nondivisible variant witnesses range over I∖{x}, not I°.
reconstruction: The corrected semantic formula Ixz=Jxz follows the unambiguous dichotomy and scan23, but the printed uncertain formula at line322 is preserved in the readings table. Transitivity is checked separately, not inferred merely from a dichotomy.
check_reason: Both entries describe the same branch-equivalence and missing-local-filtering issue; #24 supplies its proof obligation.

statement: F4: if support(I′)∩support(I″)=δI′∩δI″={z}, with z regular and other endpoints x,y, there is exactly one segment I with δI={x,y} and support(I)⊃support(I′)∪support(I″). Equality with that union is explicitly not required.
reconstruction: In the order model the omitted lieux may be incomparable with z; this interpretation is additional explanation, not a replacement of the axiom.
check_reason: The warning is explicit in two places. #21 is merged as the same substantive limitation, not treated as a second theorem.

statement: Under the preceding subdivision, branch and gluing assumptions, F5 (each regular x has exactly two branch classes) is asserted equivalent to F5′: the sets I° containing x form a filter base, meaning any two contain a third such interior.
reconstruction: The strengthened branch convention is required when formalizing the equivalence. No cardinality bound on L or S follows.
check_reason: The two formulations are present; the page announces equivalence without a complete proof.

his_words: On n’exige pas; Ou encore; I∪J⊂K
statement: Weak F6 requires, for two segments sharing endpoint x and branch there, a segment K incident to x with I°∪J°⊂K°. Strong F6 instead requires I∪J⊂K. These are not equivalent at singular other endpoints. In the poset (Q∩[0,1))⊔{u,v}, with all rationals below both incomparable maxima and all comparable-pair intervals as segments, weak F6 holds but [0,u],[0,v] have no common containing segment. If the other endpoints are regular, extension beyond them followed by weak F6 gives strong containment.
reconstruction: The named counterexample and repair are ideas of the earlier run (#40–41), independently rechecked here. They do not refute the special equal-endpoint lemma. The manuscript provides both distinct formulations and the regular-end qualification.
check_reason: The entries correctly identify a genuine hypothesis mismatch. Their examples are merged with the exact equivalence they test; all axiom checks are in audit/root_proofs.md.

statement: A réseau is the revised F1–F6 segment structure; singular lieux are nodes and regular incidence components are lines. Divisible means every I° is nonempty; reduced means every segment has support δI and Lr=∅. With branch witnesses adapted to nondivisible segments, reduced networks are simple undirected graphs S⊂P₂(L), without a finiteness assumption.
reconstruction: The graph assertion uses the explicit witness revision on scan7. Reading the earlier interior-witness clause literally would reject nonempty reduced graphs.
check_reason: #42 explicates the same definitional revision as #9; it is not evidence that the graph claim is inconsistent after the revision.

statement: A segment model with support L and two endpoints is asserted equivalent to a pair of opposite partial orders with distinct least and greatest elements, density, and local filtering in both directions: for x<y,z there is u with x<u≤y,z, and dually. Choosing the least endpoint defines x≤y by [x₀,x]⊂[x₀,y]. Segments correspond to comparable pairs with support [x,y].
reconstruction: The quantifiers use the clear strict version at scan13, not the inconsistent later mixed strict/nonstrict formula. The converse concerns the strengthened pre-F6 segment axioms, not automatically either later global F6.
check_reason: The notes correctly preserve partial rather than total order and identify the missing local hypothesis; merging avoids counting the same reconstruction twice.

his_words: voisinage fermé; Cône; espace topologique compact
statement: For closed nonempty A⊂X, regular immersion means the collapsed point a∈X/A has a closed neighborhood V homeomorphic to a cone on a compact base B, with a the vertex and V∖B open. Uniform radial subcones Vt (0<t≤1) and their open interiors form cofinal neighborhood systems; their inverse images form such a system along A.
reconstruction: The cofinality proof uses compactness of B. This is regular immersion in his terminology, not a smooth, algebraic or pointwise locally flat embedding. He explicitly adopts an apex-only cone for B=∅.
check_reason: Definition and neighborhood claim occur consecutively. #47 is the explanation of the compact-base requirement in #11.

statement: A ficelle is (X,{A,B}) with disjoint closed nonopen ends, regularly immersed in X, and connected spaces (X∖A)/B and (X∖B)/A. It is reduced if both ends are points; orientation chooses one end. Neither connectedness of each end nor connectedness of X is stipulated in the unrestricted definition.
reconstruction: The punctuation doubt in non-ouverts does not affect the negation. Nonemptiness follows because ∅ is open.
check_reason: The entry correctly resists adding the later suggested connected-end condition to the earlier definition.

statement: An internal lieu C is a closed subset disjoint from A∪B for which X∖C splits into two open-and-closed sides containing A and B, each connected after collapsing its end; C is regularly immersed in X∖(A∪B). The closed cut pieces are closure(UA,C)∪C and closure(UB,C)∪C. Ends themselves are also lieux. Simultaneous cuts must be compatible in the defined stronger sense.
reconstruction: The closure notation follows the clear scan6 notation, without deciding overwritten U/X glyphs on scan5. The finite-chain equivalence is indexed separately.
check_reason: The entry accurately combines the definition across its successive pages, retaining regular immersion and side conditions.

statement: Comp(Z) is the Boolean ring of clopen subsets of Z, with symmetric difference and intersection. Riv(A,X)=colim_{V⊃A}Comp(V∖A) under restriction as neighborhoods shrink. Its elements are germs along the whole closed set A. They are not individual connected components and need not record all link topology.
reconstruction: Boolean ring terminology restates his commutative idempotent F₂-algebra. The source uses both Riv and Rives.
check_reason: The three entries concern the same definition and the same π₀-versus-clopen correction; all are retained in one item.

statement: A birive is an unordered complementary pair β={ρ,ρ′} in Riv(A,X); for a nonzero ring its entries are distinct, and {0,1} is trivial. A maille additionally requires regular immersion and the stated ficelle conditions on the cut space; its orientation chooses one member of β. The definition replaces the earlier term boucle topologique.
reconstruction: The existence of a complementary pair alone does not establish the geometric conditions. Full-cut/partial-cut equivalence has its own claim record.
check_reason: #89 adds the terminology history to the same distinction made in #15.

statement: No atelier/workshop is defined in cotes156-1–2. Maille on 156-2/17 is a different defined object. This negative finding has only that local scope; later cotes of the current dossier do define ateliers.

his_words: I° est infini; condition de divisibilité

his_words: Cette application est injective; conditions équivalentes
statement: For S_I={J:support(J)⊂support(I)}, δ:S_I→P₂(support(I)) is injective. Its image contains all endpoint-incident pairs. An internal pair {u,v} is in the image iff v∈Ixu or v∈Iyu, equivalently u lies in the corresponding opposite initial/final subsegment based at v.

statement: If x is a regular endpoint of I with other endpoint y, F1–F4 with the strengthened branch condition imply a larger segment J with endpoint y and x∈J°. If both endpoints are regular, a larger segment has I⊂J°.

statement: For a tame category in which embedded compact arcs have finite local intersection behavior, taking all embedded arcs as segments supplies the intended F1–F4 examples. In a plane, distinct arc germs at a point need not reduce to two branches, so F5 is a real extra restriction.

his_words: partie quelc.; les axiomes F1-F5 sont satisfaits

This satisfies strengthened F1–F5 and both F6 versions. For z=(3/2,0), L′=[0,z]∪[z,3] excludes the other middle chain. z remains regular, but its two retained adjacent intervals have no retained F4 composite.

Order-convex subsets of a fixed interval-poset model give a natural sufficient setting, but a general réseau inheritance theorem requires additional branch and regularity checks.

statement: On a regular model, the equivalence relation generated by pairs lying in a common segment defines incidence components. The model is the direct sum of its components, each regular. Connectivity means connectedness of this incidence/comparability relation, without a specified topology on L.

his_words: Je n’ai pas la vérification ici; Si c’était faux

He explicitly leaves verification open and says it would need to be an axiom if false. Even the claim of one or two quotient classes is qualified.

Total comparability is not asserted. Nontransitivity is called the circular case, without a completed classification.

statement: For disjoint closed nonopen A,B, if every connected component of U=X∖(A∪B) has closure meeting both ends, then the two end-contracted punctured spaces are connected. Conversely, if U has finitely many components and those quotients are connected, each component closure must meet both ends.

statement: A ficelle is preserved by contracting a closed C⊂X∖(A∪B). Separately contracting A and B to distinct points preserves and reflects the ficelle conditions. Quotients preserve the required connectedness, and neighborhoods can be chosen off the other closed sets, leaving the local conic condition unchanged.

statement: If the ends are distinct nonisolated closed points a,b and X∖{a}, X∖{b} are connected, then X is connected: these two connected sets cover X and intersect in the nonempty interior. X∖{a,b} may be disconnected, as for a circle.

reconstruction: This distinction is used in proofs without deciding the order of pen revisions.

his_words: connexe, et non réduit à un point; unique

The first necessity fails with disconnected ends. The latter assertions hold for connected finite polyhedra, with proofs in this dossier.

statement: The stated classification A=[0,α], B=[β,1], 0≤α<β≤1 (up to exchange), requires connected ends. Under the literal definition X=[0,1], A={0,1}, B={1/2} is also a ficelle: X/A is a circle, both punctured end-contracted spaces are connected open intervals, and the ends are conical. Thus the unrestricted classification is false.
reconstruction: The counterexample is the earlier run’s idea and is independently rechecked. The connected-end repair follows because connected closed interval subsets are intervals and connectivity of punctured quotients forces the two outer ends.

statement: Enlarging the ends of a ficelle to disjoint closed regularly immersed sets need not preserve a ficelle. On a tripod take two leaves A,B, then enlarge A to its closed arm including the central vertex. The enlarged end is connected, contractible and regularly immersed, but its complement has two components and collapsing the singleton B cannot join them.
reconstruction: The author retracts the rule himself; the tripod is the earlier run’s explicit witness, checked here with all four hypotheses. It also defeats the proposed rescue by connected or contractible ends alone.
check_reason: The note reports an explicit retraction, and the companion example tests exactly the discarded rule.

his_words: soupçonne; Faux déjà dans le cas du segment!
statement: The conjecture that all oriented ficelle structures on a triangulable X are equivalent under the equivalence relation generated by coordinatewise endpoint inclusion is withdrawn. In the connected-end interval subfamily the two orientations form distinct classes, each with its minimal point-end pair. This exact count is not established for the unrestricted disconnected-end family.
reconstruction: The two-class statement is a restricted elementary reconstruction, not the author’s universal conclusion.
check_reason: The note accurately preserves both the withdrawal and the limited scope of its explanatory count.

statement: To retain the cutting-order properties after restricting endpoints and lieux by an intrinsic property P, the author proposes also requiring P for the boundary of each relevant conic neighborhood on both sides. A uniform sufficient theorem for arbitrary P is not formulated or proved.
reconstruction: A precise future formulation must specify a category and closure conditions on P under the actual collar/refinement operations.
check_reason: The entry correctly treats suggested sufficient hypotheses as a program, not an established all-P theorem.

his_words: être ... réduit à un pt; segments top.
statement: Choosing P=being a point is said to give a theory of topological segments. The strongest secure reading is a special cutting theory with point ends, allowed lieux and side links, not an automatic classification of every ambient X as an interval.
reconstruction: The final abbreviation ord./ind. is left uncertain. A connected-end pair alone would allow, for example, many noninterval spaces.
check_reason: The note appropriately avoids expanding an illustrative sentence into a global classification theorem.

statement: Ball-shaped and sphere-shaped admissible loci illustrate the property-P cutting theory in I×B^n and in S^{n+1} with two marked points. Every proposed locus must still satisfy the separating-side and regular-immersion conditions; its abstract homeomorphism type alone is insufficient.

statement: A bicollar C×(−1,1), with its two half-products in the two cut pieces, is offered as an additional condition on an internal lieu. It is stronger than the original condition on a cone neighborhood after collapsing the entire C.
reconstruction: A cone on three points distinguishes conical from interval neighborhoods at a vertex, but does not by itself provide an internal-lieu counterexample; the note explicitly says so.
check_reason: The source’s optional phrasing and the limited role of the explanatory example are correctly retained.

statement: For a regular immersion with a chosen compact cone base S, the rive algebra is canonically identified through that conic structure with Clop(S). Cofinal punctured cones are S×(0,t), and a clopen subset is constant along each connected radial fiber.
reconstruction: The abstract germ algebra is intrinsic, but no uniqueness theorem for the topological type of every possible cone base is asserted.
check_reason: The note gives a valid local product/cofinality proof strategy and avoids recovering the whole link from its clopens.

statement: For a closed A in a paracompact Hausdorff X and a sheaf of k-modules F, the restriction map colim_{V⊃A}Γ(V,F)→Γ(A,F|A) is an isomorphism. It is injective without the paracompact hypothesis. Applied to i_*F₂ on X, it compares the rive ring to sections on A; interpreting Comp(Ã) additionally requires a precise relative spectrum convention.
reconstruction: Hausdorffness is explicit in the opened modern sheaf reference’s convention. Its theorem verifies the section comparison, not every unspoken topological property of the manuscript’s cut space.
check_reason: The note correctly narrows the cited standard theorem to closed A and distinguishes the spectrum interpretation.

statement: The page leaves the base of Spec implicit. A modern relative ringed-space spectrum over X, restricted above A, retains the map to A needed by the subsequent pushouts. For X=S¹×[−1,1], A=S¹×{0}, this relative Stone boundary is two circles; the étalé space of ring elements is four circles; Spec of the global rive algebra F₂² is two points.
reconstruction: The relative-spectrum formalization and the cylinder test belong to the earlier run and are rechecked here. They are not a decision about the manuscript’s intended missing convention.
check_reason: The definition gap and its diagnostic example concern one issue. The two-circle/four-circle/two-point distinction is mathematically correct.

his_words: nulle ssi A est ouvert; ρ+ρ′=1
statement: For closed A, Riv(A,X) is the zero ring iff A is open: 0=1 in the filtered colimit iff some neighborhood has empty complement of A. In a nonzero Boolean ring, ρ and 1+ρ are distinct and define complementary clopens in its Stone spectrum; {0,1} is the trivial pair.
reconstruction: This uses the zero-ring convention explicitly allowed on the page. A birive alone does not satisfy the geometric maille axioms.
check_reason: The elementary Boolean checks agree with the note and are rerun in code/root_checks.py.

statement: For two points A={p,q} in R², disjoint punctured-disk neighborhoods give Riv(A,R²)=F₂². A nontrivial global birive exists although each individual punctured disk is connected. Thus the author’s whole-A germ disconnection need not be pointwise separation at every a∈A.
reconstruction: This is the earlier run’s diagnostic counterexample. It is not asserted to be a maille.
check_reason: The example tests the actual global germ definition and respects its additional geometric requirements.

statement: The cone vertex on Cantor space has compact link but an infinite Boolean algebra of clopen germs: the cylinder clopen partitions have unbounded finite size. Compactness alone does not imply finitely many rives.
reconstruction: This example belongs to the earlier run, not the manuscript. It does not refute a separately imposed tame finiteness hypothesis.
check_reason: The claimed obstruction follows directly from the verified conic-link computation.

statement: Cone vertices with links S¹ and S² have the same rive ring F₂ because both links are connected, although their links have different homotopy types. The Boolean side algebra alone cannot reconstruct the full link.
reconstruction: The earlier run’s example is bounded to this invariant and says nothing about equivalence of all enriched cuttings.
check_reason: The note correctly limits the negative conclusion to information actually forgotten.

statement: The parenthesis asserts transfer of regular immersion from A⊂X to the full cut boundary and its two clopen parts. A doubtful marginal réciproq. may ask for a converse. A well-defined spectrum/cut model is needed before either direction becomes a precise theorem.
reconstruction: No converse is manufactured from the abbreviation. The conic case is a test setting, not a resolution of the full unformalized assertion.
check_reason: The note keeps proof status and uncertain marginal scope separate.

statement: For a chosen birive, the proposed partial cut is the pushout which maps each of the two full spectral boundary pieces to a separate copy of A. Its map to X is asserted to be an isomorphism off A and to have the two marked copies Aρ,Aρ′ over A.
reconstruction: The source’s pushout is retained literally. Its topology and embedding properties require a specified full-cut model; no universal maille conclusion follows from its set of fibers.
check_reason: The note accurately preserves the two whole copies and avoids collapsing the side labels.

statement: The author asserts that (A,β) is a one-node maille iff its partial cut with the two copies of A is a ficelle. This depends on regular-immersion and connectivity transfer between full and partial cuts. After admissibility, orientation is the choice of ρ∈β.
reconstruction: The iff is a substantive equivalence, not merely a renaming of the earlier full-cut definition.
check_reason: The note correctly retains the unproved geometric transfer obligation.

his_words: se réduire au cas A₁,A₂ réduits à un point
statement: A marginal note suggests reducing nodes to points, but its opening and attachment are uncertain. Contraction preserves a node’s complement yet may change ambient connectedness and the connectedness of sides involving other contracted nodes; a blanket retroactive reduction is not warranted.
reconstruction: The scope restriction is an editorial/mathematical caution, not a changed reading.
check_reason: The note correctly refuses to turn a doubtful marginal suggestion into a general reduction theorem.

his_words: définit à la fois β₁ et β₂; symétrique
statement: Two node-and-birive structures must have disjoint nodes, the second node must be a lieu after the first partial cut, and the resulting two sides must induce both given birives. The author asserts symmetry on exchange of the nodes; the text ends without proof. For disconnected nodes, the phrase “two connected components” requires qualification because earlier axioms ensure quotient connectedness.
reconstruction: Simultaneous cutting is a possible proof method, not a construction supplied in these pages. The word comparables/compatibles stays uncertain.
check_reason: The definition and its immediately following symmetry assertion are consolidated with the exact unfinished endpoint.

statement: Every Boolean ring R is the filtered union of its finite Boolean subalgebras; n generators have at most 2^n atoms and at most 2^(2^n) elements. Spec R is a profinite space, the inverse limit of the finite discrete spectra of these subalgebras. For R=Riv(A,X), this reconstructs the global Stone spectrum only, not the relative boundary above A or X.
reconstruction: The profinite consequence is the earlier run’s deduction from standard Boolean duality, independently checked here. It is not a manuscript theorem about forms.
check_reason: #113 repeats and limits #96’s same positive comparison. The atom bound, not a bound of 2^n on the algebra’s elements, is the correct count.

statement: Every connected finite polyhedron with more than one point admits a reduced ficelle. Choose two leaf vertices of a spanning tree of a finite triangulation’s one-skeleton. Removing either leaves the tree on the other vertices connected, and every punctured simplex attaches to those vertices. Small closed vertex stars are compact-base cones; neither endpoint is isolated.
reconstruction: This is the earlier run’s elementary proof, re-proved here. It establishes the manuscript’s sufficiency in the finite-polyhedron setting, not a convention-independent assertion for all infinite triangulations.
check_reason: The source announces the result without this proof; attribution and bounded scope are retained.

his_words: Si X est un segment cette str. est unique
statement: A connected nontrivial finite polyhedron has a unique unordered reduced-ficelle endpoint pair iff it is homeomorphic to [0,1]. In dimension≥2 there are infinitely many conical noncut interior points of a maximal simplex. A graph with a cycle also has infinitely many noncut points; a finite tree has precisely its leaves as noncut points and exactly two leaves iff it is an arc.
reconstruction: The proof is the earlier run’s, independently checked. It is about reduced structures on the fixed underlying space, not uniqueness of all disconnected-end decorations or equivalence modulo automorphisms.
check_reason: The note correctly isolates the true reduced uniqueness statement from the false unrestricted interval classification.

his_words: construction récurrente; n homeo. de raccordement
statement: The first two cotes do not define forms as a pro-object of finite posets/categories. Finite chains of geometrically labeled cuts are present, but the proposed indexing category, bonding maps and a reconstruction equivalence are absent from this package.
reconstruction: This tests the earlier context’s title-based conjecture, not a conjecture stated by Grothendieck here. The later ateliers are considered separately.
check_reason: The note’s limited absence claim agrees with the full package; it must not be globalized to later cotes.

statement: Compatible chains ordered by retaining literal embedded cuts and adding new ones need not be directed. In a square with opposite vertical ends, a vertical cut and a small tilted cut are each admissible collared lieux but intersect. Even disjoint sets can fail compatibility: on a circle with ends a,b, take two-point separators at arc-coordinates (1/3,2/3) and (2/3,1/3); each is a lieu, but the second straddles both sides of the first.
reconstruction: Both are earlier-run counterexamples to a particular proposed refinement order, not to a refinement category allowing isotopy, replacements or subdivided intersections. All ficelle and cone hypotheses are checked in audit/root_proofs.md.
check_reason: The two examples test the same directedness overclaim while distinguishing crossing from merely incompatible disjoint cuts.

statement: A pro-object proposal requires a specified cofiltered category, objects of the target category, and functorial bonding maps, together with a specified reconstruction functor and equivalence notion. The finite number of cuts in each object supplies none of these global requirements by itself.
reconstruction: This is the earlier run’s formal research specification, not a construction found in the manuscript.
check_reason: The note accurately lists missing data and makes no positive pro-object theorem claim.

statement: A directed inverse limit in Top of finite T₀ spaces and continuous bonding maps is spectral. If that limit is Hausdorff, its compact open basis is clopen, so a nontrivial connected Hausdorff space cannot be such a raw limit. This does not exclude a quotient of the limit or a weak/homotopy comparison.
reconstruction: This is a standard-theorem deduction of the earlier run. Finite T₀ spaces are sober; continuous maps between finite spaces are spectral because every subset is quasicompact.
check_reason: The conclusion has the precise restricted interpretation stated in the note; no general impossibility of finite models follows.

statement: Finite T₀ spaces/posets can model the weak homotopy types of finite simplicial complexes via McCord’s finite-space/order-complex comparison. A finite non-discrete poset is not equivalent to a finite discrete set for this purpose.
reconstruction: The literature comparison belongs to the earlier run, not Grothendieck’s page; a manuscript-specific finite model and comparison map still need construction.
check_reason: The note correctly separates weak homotopy reconstruction from homeomorphism.

statement: Clader’s inverse system from iterated barycentric face-posets has an inverse limit homotopy equivalent to a finite simplicial complex and a quotient homeomorphic to it. The 2016 erratum repairs the continuity proof. No identification with Grothendieck’s compatible ficelle-cut chains is supplied.
reconstruction: This is an external comparison, with the correction included; both raw-limit and quotient conclusions must be distinguished.
check_reason: The note’s modern result is verified against the opened paper and erratum, not inferred from its title.

statement: Finite-space simple equivalences correspond to simple homotopy types of finite simplicial complexes in Barmak–Minian’s comparison. Applying that theorem to ficelle cuts would require a specified finite model and proof that the proposed geometric moves induce the required collapses/expansions.
reconstruction: The application is an earlier-run idea, not established by the cited comparison theorem or the manuscript’s gluing equivalence.
check_reason: The entry correctly states a research target with a missing comparison functor.

statement: The fully faithful exit-path construction in conically smooth stratified homotopy theory retains mapping-space/link information. It supplies a comparison framework under its own geometric hypotheses, not a theorem that an ordinary finite incidence category determines any ficelle up to homeomorphism.

check_reason: The note accurately preserves the modern theorem’s enriched and hypothesis-dependent scope.

statement: Esquisse §5 discusses reconstruction using a boundary-bearing piece, a closed stratum and an attaching map, expressed as a pushout. This is a concrete conceptual parallel to the retained end spaces and gluing maps of ficelle cuts.
reconstruction: The parallel is an inference, not an exact theorem identifying the two constructions or defining an atelier in cotes1–2.
check_reason: The note’s limited geometric comparison is supported by the opened primary text.

statement: Replacing gluing homeomorphisms by isotopy classes is an additional quotient operation. Esquisse §5, printed pp29–30, distinguishes the induced map on isotopy classes from the stronger homotopy-equivalence statement about isomorphism spaces; a cutting theory must specify which coherence data survive that replacement.
reconstruction: This is an earlier-run research question, not an established deficiency of a particular constructed enhanced category.
check_reason: The source comparison is real, while the application remains explicitly unconstructed. The earlier note’s §6 locator is corrected to §5, printed pp29–30, for the Isom_T to Isom_T′ map.

statement: Finitely many cuts per object do not make the category of geometric cutting data finite. General finite categories also have endomorphism and automorphism data absent from posets; extending a poset comparison therefore requires a separate theorem.
reconstruction: This logical distinction belongs to the earlier run. Some other-project endpoints invoked in its Context paragraph were recovered in neighbouring context selections; their exact scope and access limits are recorded separately in SA21_project_leads.tsv. None supplies the missing extension theorem.
check_reason: The note makes no unsupported extension theorem and is kept with its contextual leads segregated.

statement: For Y=S¹ or S², the product ficelle Y×[0,1] with end fibers and chosen horizontal fiber cuts has the same abstract finite chain of cut indices for any selected times. The labeled pieces retain different homotopy types. Thus forgetting those labels loses information.
reconstruction: This earlier-run example does not assert that the full posets of all lieux in the two products are isomorphic.
check_reason: The note’s bounded information-loss conclusion is correct and independently checked.
